Each two-channel block uses four cascaded MZIs (30 µm, 50 µm, 30 µm, 50 µm path differences), with 2×2 MMIs as splitters/combiners. Arrange them so that channels 1 and 2 are separated by the first two-channel block, channels 3 and 4 by the second block, and then route all outputs to the final block to generate four distinct outputs. The final device should have 4 inputs and 4 outputs.

Design an optical 64-QAM transmitter that encodes 6 bits per symbol using exactly three dual-drive Mach-Zehnder Modulators (MZM). Each MZM has 1 optical input port and 1 optical output port, and two RF input drives for phase control. Use two 1×2 multimode interferometer (MMIs) to split a single input optical signal equally into three paths for the parallel MZMs. Ensure each mzm_dual modulates two of the six total bits by adjusting the phase via its dual RF drives. After modulation, recombine the three optical outputs using two 2×1 MMIs to produce the 64-QAM output signal, where amplitude and phase both vary.

Design an optical 8-QAM transmitter that encodes 3 bits per symbol using exactly three single-drive Mach-Zehnder Modulators (mzm), each with 1 optical input port, 1 optical output port, and a single RF drive. Use two 1×2 MMIs to split a single input optical signal into three branches. Assign one bit to each mzm, and specify the necessary phase shifts or bias points to achieve the desired 8-QAM (amplitude and phase) modulation on each branch. Finally, use two 2×1 MMIs to combine the three modulated signals into the final 8-QAM output.

Ensure that the final design places all 8 input ports on one side and all 8 output ports on the other, with correct inter-stage connectivity to realize a full Benes network.

Design a Non-Linear Sign (NLS) gate with one signal and two ancilla channels (three inputs, three outputs) using three 2x2 MMI couplers and a phase shifter. The signal channel passes through a phase shifter (ϕ = 180°) before entering MMI 1, inducing the required nonlinear sign flip. MMI 1 combines the phase-shifted signal with one ancilla, while MMI 2 couples the second ancilla and feeds both MMI 1 and MMI 3. MMI 3 recombines outputs from MMIs 1 and 2 to realize the NLS logic operation.

Design a 2x2 optical switch using built-in coupler components and phase shifters. By incorporating 4 built-in multimode interferometer (MMI) components and 4 adjustable phase shifters, the switch should be able to alternate between the cross and bar states, effectively controlling the switching operation.

Design a 90-degree optical hybrid using two inputs (LO and signal) and four outputs (I, Q, -I, -Q). First, use built-in 1×2 MMI components to split each input into two equal paths. Introduce a 90° phase shifter on one of the LO paths while leaving the other LO path unshifted. Next, use 2x2 directional couplers to mix the shifted and unshifted LO paths with the two split signal paths. Configure these mixing stages so that the four final outputs are I, Q, -I, and -Q.

Design an optical QPSK modulator using single drive Mach-Zehnder Modulators (MZMs) to encode 2 bits per symbol through phase modulation. The circuit should have only one input and one output, and employ the MZMs to modulate the in-phase (I) and quadrature-phase (Q) components of the signal. A 90-degree phase shifter should be used in the path of one of the MZMs, ensuring that the modulation is performed at the correct quadrature points for accurate QPSK encoding. Use the built-in multimode interferometer (MMI) component for splitting and combining the optical signals, and a built-in components called mzm to represent the single drive Mach-Zehnder modulators.

Design an optical WDM demultiplexer that separates a composite optical signal into 4 individual wavelength channels for processing and analysis. The multiplexer will utilize a series of built-in add/drop Micro Ring Resonators to efficiently extract 4 distinct wavelength channels from a single input fiber. The design will ensure precise alignment of the optical paths to effectively isolate and direct each wavelength to its designated output port. The circuit should only have one input and one output.

Design an optical WDM multiplexer that combines 4 channels of optical signals, each at a distinct wavelength, into a single optical fiber for transmission. The multiplexer will utilize a series of built-in add/drop Micro Ring Resonators, each operating at a unique wavelength. The output will be a composite optical signal encompassing all 4 wavelengths, enabling simultaneous transmission of multiple data channels over a single fiber. The circuit should have 4 inputs for each input signal and only one output.
